title: Payment service slow responses
executive_summary: Payment-service slowness (p99 ~300ms to ~3.4s, timeouts 0.1% to ~6%) is caused by auth-service degradation. auth-service p99 rose from 86ms to ~3.3s at 18:07-18:10, its error rate rose to ~2.9%, and CPU went from 30% to ~47%, with request-queue waits of 2-10s on /v1/token/verify. Payment logs show 3000ms upstream timeouts to auth-service starting at 18:10:19. Request volume was flat, so this is not a traffic surge. The probable trigger is slow JWKS refresh from identity-provider (120-970ms, first at 18:06:12), but this is not confirmed. Payment's own resources and error rate were unchanged.

hypotheses.description: auth-service is saturated or queueing on /v1/token/verify, and payment-service times out waiting on it. Mechanism: auth-service CPU rose ~30% to ~47% at 18:10 with flat request rate. Its request queue time reached 2-10s, so calls from payment exceed the 3000ms timeout and fail. Payment's latency and timeouts follow auth's degradation.

hypotheses.description: A slowdown at the external identity provider degrades auth-service JWKS refresh, which starves or stalls token verification. Mechanism: JWKS refresh calls to identity-provider slowed from 18:06 (120-970ms). Verification of tokens may block on refresh or on shared resources, and this starts auth degradation about 4 minutes before payment is affected.

probable_root_cause.description: auth-service is saturated or queueing on /v1/token/verify, and payment-service times out waiting on it.
probable_root_cause.label: MOST PROBABLE EXPLANATION (INFERENCE, not confirmed)

root_cause_statement: MOST PROBABLE EXPLANATION (INFERENCE, not confirmed): upstream_dependency_degradation in auth-service - auth-service is saturated or queueing on /v1/token/verify, and payment-service times out waiting on it.
corrective_actions: Mitigate now: raise or relax the payment->auth timeout (3000ms) with a circuit breaker, or fail over token verification to a cached/local JWT validation path.
Scale auth-service or relieve its verify queue (add replicas, or shed load) to stop the queue growth.
Investigate the identity-provider JWKS slowdown and extend the JWKS cache TTL so verification stops depending on live refresh.
preventive_actions: Add timeouts, retries budgets and circuit breakers around auth-service calls from payment-service.
Make JWKS refresh asynchronous with stale-while-revalidate, so identity-provider slowness cannot block token verification.
Alert on auth-service queue time and CPU, not only error rate.
monitoring_recommendations: Alert on auth-service /v1/token/verify queue time > 500ms and p99 > 500ms.
Track identity-provider latency and JWKS refresh duration as a dashboard panel.
Alert on payment-service to auth-service timeout rate > 0.5%.
limitations: The causal link from JWKS refresh to auth saturation is inferred, not proven.
Historical incident HIST-2025-031 is an analogy only.
The order of onset (JWKS 18:06, auth 18:07, payment 18:09-18:10) is based on 5-minute sampled metrics plus log timestamps.
[agent-reported gap] No telemetry for identity-provider itself.
[agent-reported gap] No thread-pool or event-loop metrics for auth-service.
[agent-reported gap] No payment log volume data around the 17:35 DEBUG change.
[agent-reported gap] Payment dashboard pods looked healthy, but the cause is in auth-service.
Confidence values are rule-based evidence-strength scores, not calibrated probabilities.
conclusion: Payment-service latency and timeouts are downstream effects of degraded auth-service. auth-service p99 and error rate rose ~7 minutes before payment-service p99 did, auth-service CPU rose at the same time, and payment's timeouts are specifically 3000ms timeouts calling auth-service /v1/token/verify. Payment's own CPU, DB connection utilisation and error rate were flat. The trigger inside auth-service is not fully confirmed: slow JWKS refreshes from identity-provider began at 18:06 and match a past incident, but the magnitudes are modest and auth CPU growth is not fully explained by them.
